questions.q: In which state of matter are the forces of attraction between particles the weakest?
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart, so the attraction between them is weakest.

questions.q: At normal atmospheric pressure, water boils at
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C, which is 373 K.

questions.q: The smell of hot food reaches us from the kitchen even from a distance because of
questions.explanation: Particles of the aroma mix with air particles on their own, which is diffusion.

questions.q: The heat energy needed to change 1 kg of a liquid into gas at its boiling point, without any rise in temperature, is called
questions.explanation: This hidden heat is the latent heat of vaporisation.

questions.q: Solid carbon dioxide is called dry ice because it
options: changes directly from solid to gas without becoming a liquid
is frozen water with no moisture
is carbon dioxide dissolved in ice
is ice stored in dry air
questions.explanation: It sublimes at normal pressure and leaves no liquid behind.

questions.q: A syringe full of air can be pressed in easily, but a syringe full of water cannot. This is because
options: water particles are lighter than air particles
the spaces between air particles are large, but those between liquid particles are very small
air has less mass than water
questions.explanation: Air can be compressed into its large spaces; liquids are nearly incompressible.

questions.q: Steam at 100 °C causes more severe burns than boiling water at 100 °C because steam
options: carries extra latent heat of vaporisation that is released when it condenses on the skin
is at a higher temperature than 100 °C
questions.explanation: Condensing steam gives out latent heat in addition to the heat from cooling.

questions.q: Write two differences between boiling and evaporation.
questions.answer: Boiling takes place throughout the liquid at one fixed temperature, the boiling point, and is a bulk phenomenon. Evaporation occurs only at the surface, at any temperature below the boiling point, and is a slow process.
keyPoints: Boiling occurs at a fixed temperature
Boiling is throughout the liquid; evaporation is at the surface
questions.explanation: Both change a liquid into vapour but under different conditions.

questions.q: Why are cotton clothes preferred in summer?
questions.answer: Cotton absorbs sweat and exposes it to the air over a large surface, so the sweat evaporates quickly. Evaporation takes heat from the body and keeps us cool.
questions.explanation: Synthetic fabrics absorb little sweat, so they cool less.

questions.q: Which of the following is an element?
questions.explanation: Sulphur consists of only one kind of atom.

questions.q: In a solution of common salt in water, the salt is called the
questions.explanation: The substance that dissolves is the solute; water is the solvent.

questions.q: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance, iron oxide.

questions.q: 20 g of common salt is dissolved in 80 g of water. The mass percentage of the solution is
questions.explanation: Mass percentage = 20 / (20 + 80) × 100 = 20%.

questions.q: The different dyes present in black ink can be separated by
questions.explanation: Different dyes travel at different rates on the paper in chromatography.

questions.q: Which method is best for getting pure crystals of copper sulphate from its impure solution?
questions.explanation: On cooling a hot saturated solution, pure crystals form and impurities stay in solution.

questions.q: Nitrogen and oxygen of the air can be separated industrially by
options: fractional distillation of liquid air, using their different boiling points
evaporation of air at room temperature
questions.explanation: Air is cooled to a liquid and its gases boil off at different temperatures.

questions.q: Differentiate between a homogeneous and a heterogeneous mixture, giving one example of each.
questions.answer: A homogeneous mixture has uniform composition throughout, for example salt solution. A heterogeneous mixture has non-uniform composition with visible parts, for example sand and water.
questions.explanation: The difference lies in how uniformly the components are mixed.

questions.q: Is air a compound or a mixture? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: Air is a mixture. Its components (nitrogen, oxygen, etc.) are present in no fixed ratio that varies slightly from place to place, and each keeps its own properties. They can be separated by physical methods such as fractional distillation of liquid air.
questions.explanation: A compound would have fixed composition and properties unlike its elements.

questions.q: How many atoms are present in a molecule of oxygen, O2?
questions.explanation: The subscript 2 shows two atoms; oxygen is diatomic.

questions.q: The chemical formula of sodium chloride is
questions.explanation: Sodium has valency 1 and chlorine has valency 1, so they combine one to one.

questions.q: According to Dalton's atomic theory, atoms
options: can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
can be divided into electrons and protons
can be seen with a simple microscope
questions.explanation: Dalton proposed that atoms are the basic indivisible particles and are only rearranged in reactions.

questions.q: The chemical formula of aluminium oxide is
questions.explanation: Al has valency 3 and O has valency 2; criss-crossing gives Al2O3.

questions.q: The mass of 1 mole of oxygen atoms is (atomic mass of O = 16 u)
questions.explanation: One mole of atoms has a mass equal to the atomic mass expressed in grams.

questions.q: One mole of carbon dioxide molecules contains how many moles of atoms?
questions.explanation: Each CO2 molecule has 1 carbon and 2 oxygen atoms, so there are 3 moles of atoms.

questions.q: In water, hydrogen and oxygen combine in the ratio 1 : 8 by mass. How much hydrogen is present in 18 g of water?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is 1/9 of the mass, so 18 × 1/9 = 2 g.

questions.q: Write the chemical formulae of calcium chloride and magnesium hydroxide.
questions.answer: Calcium has valency 2 and chloride has valency 1, so calcium chloride is CaCl2. Magnesium has valency 2 and hydroxide has valency 1, so magnesium hydroxide is Mg(OH)2.
questions.explanation: The formula balances the positive and negative charges.

questions.q: Calculate the molar mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO3, and the mass of 0.2 mole of it. (Ca = 40 u, C = 12 u, O = 16 u)
questions.answer: Molar mass = 40 + 12 + 3 × 16 = 100 g/mol. Mass of 0.2 mole = 0.2 × 100 = 20 g.
questions.explanation: Mass of a sample is the number of moles times the molar mass.

questions.q: Who proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain fixed shells?
questions.explanation: Bohr proposed that electrons stay in discrete orbits without radiating energy.

questions.q: The mass of an electron compared with that of a proton is
questions.explanation: A proton is about 1836 times heavier than an electron.

questions.q: A proton carries a
questions.explanation: Protons carry one unit of positive charge.

questions.q: The mass number of an atom is the
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons make up almost all the mass; together they are called nucleons.

questions.q: How many neutrons are present in an atom of carbon-14 (atomic number 6)?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 14 − 6 = 8.

questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ only in the number of neutrons, so their atomic number stays the same.

questions.q: An atom has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8. This atom is
options: chemically inert because its outermost shell is complete
questions.explanation: An octet in the outermost shell makes the atom stable, like argon.

questions.q: Write the electronic configuration and valency of magnesium (atomic number 12).
questions.answer: The electronic configuration is 2, 8, 2. Magnesium has two electrons in its outermost shell, which it can lose, so its valency is 2.
questions.explanation: Valency is the number of electrons lost, gained or shared to reach a full outer shell.

questions.q: Why do isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties but different physical properties?
questions.answer: Chemical properties depend on the number and arrangement of electrons, which is the same for isotopes. Physical properties such as density and mass depend on the number of neutrons, which differs.
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ in mass number but not in atomic number.

questions.q: Proteins are made in the cell by small structures called
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

questions.q: Which part of the cell controls all its activities and contains the chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The nucleus directs the cell's activities and carries genetic material.

questions.q: The green plastids that carry out photosynthesis are called
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll.

questions.q: Which of the following cells has no cell wall?
questions.explanation: Animal cells are bounded only by the plasma membrane.

questions.q: Rough endoplasmic reticulum looks rough because
options: ribosomes are attached to its surface
it is covered with fat droplets
questions.explanation: Ribosomes on its surface give a rough appearance.

questions.q: The Golgi apparatus is mainly concerned with
options: storage, modification and packaging of substances
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages substances made in the ER for transport.

questions.q: A plant cell placed in pure water swells but does not burst, unlike an animal cell, because the plant cell has
questions.explanation: The strong cell wall resists the pressure of the water that enters.

questions.q: State two functions of the plasma membrane.
questions.answer: The plasma membrane encloses the cell contents and separates the cell from its surroundings. It is selectively permeable, so it controls which substances enter and leave the cell.
keyPoints: Controls entry and exit of substances
questions.explanation: It acts as the cell's boundary and gatekeeper.

questions.q: Why do muscle cells contain a large number of mitochondria?
questions.answer: Muscle cells are very active and need a lot of energy for contraction. Mitochondria release energy from food as ATP, so more mitochondria supply more energy.
keyPoints: Muscle cells need a lot of energy
questions.explanation: Number of mitochondria matches the energy needs of a cell.

questions.q: Fat is stored in the body in which tissue?
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is a connective tissue that stores fat.

questions.q: Which tissue forms the protective covering of the skin and the lining of the mouth?
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissues cover and line the body and its organs.

questions.q: Blood is a type of
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue that connects and transports.

questions.q: Which of the following is a component of phloem?
questions.explanation: Sieve tubes carry food in phloem; tracheids and vessels belong to xylem.

questions.q: In aquatic plants, parenchyma with large air cavities that helps them float is called
questions.explanation: Aerenchyma has air spaces that give buoyancy.

questions.q: Which muscle cells are long, cylindrical, unbranched, striped and have many nuclei?
questions.explanation: These are the features of skeletal muscle fibres.

questions.q: The tissue found at the joints that smoothens the bone surfaces and is also found in the nose, ear and trachea is
questions.explanation: Cartilage is a smooth, flexible connective tissue.

questions.q: How does a ligament differ from a tendon?
questions.answer: A ligament connects one bone to another bone and is elastic, while a tendon connects muscle to bone and is strong with little elasticity.
questions.explanation: Both are connective tissues but they join different structures.

questions.q: Why are the cells of the epithelium of the skin tightly packed with very little intercellular space?
questions.answer: The skin epithelium forms a barrier that protects the body from injury, germs and loss of water. Tightly packed cells leave no gaps through which these could pass.
keyPoints: No gaps for germs or water loss
questions.explanation: Structure suits function: protection needs a continuous layer.

questions.q: Speed is calculated as
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time.

questions.q: A body that covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, however small the intervals, is said to be in
questions.explanation: Equal distances in equal times is uniform motion.

questions.q: The device in a vehicle that records the distance travelled is the
questions.explanation: The odometer shows the distance covered.

questions.q: A straight sloping line in a velocity-time graph indicates
questions.explanation: A constant slope means the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal times.

questions.q: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the
questions.explanation: Area under the velocity-time graph equals displacement.

questions.q: A car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s². The distance covered in 3 s is
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 4 × 9 = 18 m.

questions.q: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a circle at a constant speed. Its velocity is changing because
options: its direction of motion keeps changing
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, so a change in direction means a change in velocity.

questions.q: Write the three equations of uniformly accelerated motion.
questions.answer: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as, where u is initial velocity, v is final velocity, a is acceleration, t is time and s is displacement.
questions.explanation: They hold when acceleration is constant.

questions.q: A cyclist rides 6 km at 12 km/h and then another 6 km at 4 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.answer: Time for the first part = 6/12 = 0.5 h; time for the second part = 6/4 = 1.5 h. Total distance = 12 km, total time = 2 h, so average speed = 12/2 = 6 km/h.
keyPoints: Time = distance / speed for each part
Average speed = total distance / total time = 6 km/h
questions.explanation: Average speed is not the simple average of the two speeds (8 km/h).

questions.q: The inertia of a body depends on its
questions.explanation: Greater mass means greater inertia.

questions.q: According to Newton's third law, the action and reaction forces are
options: equal in magnitude and in the same direction
equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
questions.explanation: They are equal and opposite and act on two different bodies.

questions.q: If the net force on an object that is at rest is zero, the object will
questions.explanation: Without an unbalanced force the state of rest does not change.

questions.q: The momentum of a 3 kg object moving at 4 m/s is
questions.explanation: p = mv = 3 × 4 = 12 kg m/s.

questions.q: Which of the following has the greatest inertia?
questions.explanation: The loaded truck has the greatest mass.

questions.q: A 1000 kg car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s. The net force on it is
A 5 kg trolley moving at 2 m/s hits an identical stationary 5 kg trolley and they move together. Their common velocity is
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 5 × 2 = (5 + 5) × v, so v = 1 m/s.

questions.q: Define inertia and give one example of inertia of rest.
questions.answer: Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of rest or of uniform motion. Example: when a card under a coin on a glass is flicked away, the coin drops into the glass because it tends to stay at rest.
questions.explanation: The greater the mass of a body, the greater its inertia.

questions.q: Using Newton's third law, explain how a swimmer moves forward.
questions.answer: The swimmer pushes the water backward with her hands and feet (action). The water pushes the swimmer forward with an equal and opposite force (reaction), so she moves forward.
questions.explanation: Action and reaction act on different bodies, so the swimmer can accelerate.

questions.q: The universal law of gravitation was given by
questions.explanation: Newton proposed the universal law of gravitation.

questions.q: The SI unit of the universal gravitational constant G is
questions.explanation: From F = G m1 m2 / r², the unit of G is N m² kg⁻².

questions.q: An object is dropped from rest and falls freely for 2 s. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², its velocity after 2 s is
A body floats in a liquid when the density of the body is
options: much greater than that of the liquid
greater than that of the liquid
four times that of the liquid
less than that of the liquid
questions.explanation: If the body is less dense than the liquid, the upthrust exceeds its weight.

questions.q: It is easier to float in sea water than in river water because sea water
options: is denser and so exerts a larger upthrust for the same displaced volume
questions.explanation: Upthrust = density of liquid × volume displaced × g, so a denser liquid gives more upthrust.

questions.q: A person weighs 600 N on Earth. If the Moon's gravity is one-sixth of the Earth's, the person's weight on the Moon is
questions.explanation: Weight on the Moon = 600 / 6 = 100 N.

questions.q: Write two differences between mass and weight.
questions.answer: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body; it is constant everywhere and is measured in kilograms. Weight is the force with which the Earth attracts the body; it changes from place to place and is measured in newtons.
keyPoints: Mass in kg, weight in N
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × g, so it depends on the local g.

questions.q: Why does a steel ship float while a steel needle sinks?
questions.answer: The hull of the ship is hollow and shaped to displace a large volume of water, so the upthrust equals its weight and its average density is less than that of water. A needle displaces little water, so the upthrust is less than its weight.
keyPoints: Ship displaces large volume of water
questions.explanation: Floating depends on the average density and the volume of liquid displaced.

questions.q: In science, work done on an object is equal to
options: force times displacement in the direction of the force
questions.explanation: W = F × s when the displacement is along the force.

questions.q: The SI unit of power is the
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

questions.q: The energy stored in a stretched rubber band is
questions.explanation: A stretched band has stored (elastic potential) energy.

questions.q: A man does 600 J of work in 20 s. His power is
questions.explanation: Power = work / time = 600 / 20 = 30 W.

questions.q: In a solar cell, the energy conversion is from
questions.explanation: Solar cells convert sunlight into electricity.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward. At its highest point
options: kinetic energy is maximum and potential energy is zero
kinetic energy is zero and potential energy is maximum
questions.explanation: The ball is momentarily at rest at the top, so all its energy there is potential.

questions.q: Define 1 joule of work.
questions.answer: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 metre in the direction of the force.

questions.q: A force of 20 N moves a block 5 m along a smooth horizontal floor in the direction of the force. Find the work done and the kinetic energy gained if the block starts from rest.
questions.answer: Work done = 20 × 5 = 100 J. By the work-energy theorem all of this becomes kinetic energy, since the floor is smooth, so the gain in kinetic energy is 100 J.
keyPoints: Smooth floor so no energy lost to friction
questions.explanation: Work done on the block equals its gain in kinetic energy.

questions.q: The repeated hearing of a sound after reflection from a distant surface is called
questions.explanation: A reflected sound heard separately is an echo.

questions.q: Loudness of sound is measured in
questions.explanation: The decibel (dB) is the unit of sound level.

questions.q: A sound wave of frequency 50 Hz travels at 340 m/s. Its wavelength is
Sound of frequency above 20 000 Hz is called
questions.explanation: Sound above the human audible range is ultrasound.

questions.q: A ship sends an ultrasonic pulse down and receives the echo from the sea floor after 4 s. If the speed of sound in sea water is 1500 m/s, the depth of the sea is
questions.explanation: The pulse travels down and up, so depth = 1500 × 4 / 2 = 3000 m.

questions.q: Bats can detect obstacles in the dark by
options: emitting ultrasonic waves and detecting their echoes
questions.explanation: Bats use echolocation with ultrasound.

questions.q: What is reverberation? How can it be reduced in a big hall?
questions.answer: Reverberation is the persistence of sound in a hall due to repeated reflections from the walls and ceiling. It can be reduced by covering the walls and ceiling with sound-absorbing materials such as curtains, carpets and acoustic tiles.
keyPoints: Persistence of sound due to repeated reflection
Use of sound absorbers like curtains or carpets
questions.explanation: Excess reverberation makes speech unclear.

questions.q: Astronauts on the Moon talk to each other using radio. Why can they not talk directly as on Earth?
questions.answer: The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no air or other medium to carry sound waves. Radio waves are electromagnetic waves that can travel through a vacuum.
questions.explanation: Sound cannot pass through empty space.

questions.q: Which of the following is a commonly used chemical fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Urea is a factory-made nitrogen fertiliser; the others are organic manures.

questions.q: Which of the following is a pulse crop that is a good source of protein?
questions.explanation: Gram is a pulse; pulses give protein.

questions.q: Hybridisation in crops means crossing between
options: plants of the same variety only
questions.explanation: Hybridisation crosses genetically dissimilar plants to combine useful traits.

questions.q: Broilers are chickens raised mainly for
questions.explanation: Broilers are fed for fast growth to give meat.

questions.q: Poultry birds raised for egg production are called
questions.explanation: Layers are hens raised to lay eggs.

questions.q: Why is excessive use of chemical pesticides harmful?
options: It can pollute soil and water and enter the food chain
It helps bees to produce honey
questions.explanation: Pesticides can persist in the environment and accumulate in living things.

questions.q: Differentiate between kharif and rabi crops.
questions.answer: Kharif crops are grown in the rainy season from about June to October, for example paddy and maize. Rabi crops are grown in the winter season from about November to April, for example wheat and mustard.
questions.explanation: The two groups depend on the season and water needs.

questions.q: Name two biotic and two abiotic factors that cause losses of stored grains.
questions.answer: Biotic factors are living causes such as insects, rodents, fungi and bacteria. Abiotic factors are non-living causes such as improper moisture and temperature in the place of storage.
keyPoints: Two biotic factors such as insects and rodents
Abiotic factors are moisture and temperature
questions.explanation: Good storage controls both groups of factors.
